questions.q: What are the three activities chained together in this lesson's example pipeline?
questions.explain: Lookup reads which table to copy, Copy moves that table's data, and Stored Procedure logs the run's completion — a genuinely common real-world shape.

questions.q: What are the four dependency conditions a connection between two activities can carry?
questions.explain: Every connection on the canvas carries one of these four conditions, controlling exactly when the downstream activity actually runs.

questions.q: In this lesson's example, what dependency condition connects Copy to the Stored Procedure activity?
options: Succeeded — only log completion if the copy actually worked
Failed — only log if the copy failed
There is no dependency condition between them
questions.explain: The Stored Procedure activity only runs when Copy succeeds — logging completion only makes sense if the copy actually worked.

questions.q: What does selecting Debug on the pipeline toolbar do?
options: Runs the pipeline immediately, without publishing or waiting for a trigger
Only validates the JSON without ever running anything
questions.explain: Debug mode runs the pipeline right away for testing, showing progress directly on the canvas as each activity runs, succeeds, or fails.

questions.q: Why connect Copy to a Fail activity with a Failed dependency condition?
options: So the pipeline stops loudly with a clear message instead of silently doing nothing if the copy doesn't work
To guarantee the Copy activity always succeeds
Fail activities can only be connected to Lookup activities, never Copy
To automatically retry the Copy activity forever
questions.explain: This is the pattern from Lesson 15: failing on purpose, with an explanation, is far easier to debug than a pipeline that just quietly doesn't finish.
